packages.label: אִשָּׁה וָדֶרֶךְ
packages.reason: The Torah explicitly states 'ki isha nikret derech' — a woman is called a 'path/way' (Kiddushin 2a). Both concepts express the same essential reality: the relational channel through which the covenant is expressed and through which divine light flows (or fails to flow in the case of pgam habrit). The same identification holds in both the holy and corrupted form: the holy wife/path vs. 'derech isha mena'efet' (the way of the adulteress, Proverbs 30:20). They are neutral in polarity because the same derech-isha nexus can be holy (proper marriage, the Elul tikkun) or evil (the pgam habrit). They are two names for one structural reality: the covenant relationship as a channel/path.

packages.label: יָם וֶאֱמוּנָה
packages.reason: The Torah explicitly states 'bivchinат yam, bechinat emunah' — the yam (sea) is the bechina of emunah (faith). The 224 (rach'd) lights must shine in the 'sea,' which is identified as the dimension of faith. Both concepts express the same essential reality: the vast, boundless, receptive medium that holds divine light. The sea as a metaphor for emunah captures the quality of something that receives, contains, and extends beyond visible limits — exactly how faith functions in the soul. The kavvanot of Elul open the 'derech bа-yam,' illuminating this faith-sea. Polarity is good because the ים/אמונה nexus is the positive, receptive domain of holiness where the tikkun operates.
